test.title: Part 1–4: Cambridge IELTS 19 Academic Listening Test 3

items.quote: Well, there are plenty of places to buy food in Kite Place — it's the area by the harbour.
items.prompt: Kite Place — near the ____

explanation.en: Kite Place is identified as the area by the harbour; the bridge is a later direction to the fish market.
explanation.kk: Kite Place harbour маңында; көпір кейін балық базарына жол түсіндіргенде аталады.
explanation.ru: Kite Place расположен у гавани, harbour; мост упоминают позже при объяснении пути к рынку.

items.quote: It's at the far end of Kite Place, so you have to go over the bridge and then it's on the right.
items.prompt: Fish market: cross the ____ and turn right

explanation.en: Leon says to go over the bridge and then turn right; the harbour names the wider area.
explanation.kk: Леон bridge арқылы өтіп, оңға бұрылуды айтады; айлақ — кеңірек аймақ.
explanation.ru: Леон советует перейти мост, bridge, затем направо; гавань — название более широкой зоны.

items.quote: As long as you get there by 3.30, you should be fine.
items.prompt: Fish market: best to go before ____ pm, earlier than closing time

explanation.en: Arrive by 3.30 to avoid stock running out; four is the closing time and 11 is the current time.
explanation.kk: Тауар таусылмауы үшін 3.30-ға дейін келу керек; төрт — жабылу, он бір — қазіргі уақыт.
explanation.ru: Прийти нужно к 3.30, пока есть товар; четыре — закрытие, одиннадцать — текущее время.

items.quote: I know, it's 'Rose'.
items.prompt: Organic shop: called ____

explanation.en: Leon remembers the organic shop’s flower-based name, Rose.
explanation.kk: Леон органикалық дүкеннің гүл атауынан алынған Rose атауын еске түсіреді.
explanation.ru: Леон вспоминает цветочное название магазина органических продуктов — Rose.

items.quote: You can't miss it — there's also a big sign on the pavement so you can look for that.
items.prompt: Organic shop: look for the large ____ outside

explanation.en: A big sign on the pavement makes the organic shop easy to identify; the building is grey, not the sign.
explanation.kk: Тротуардағы үлкен sign дүкенді табуға көмектеседі; сұр түсті — белгі емес, ғимарат.
explanation.ru: Большая вывеска, sign, на тротуаре помогает найти магазин; серое — здание, а не вывеска.

items.quote: It's purple and the number is 289.
items.prompt: Supermarket: ____ minibus, number 289

explanation.en: The minibus is purple; 289 is its route number, not the colour required by the gap.
explanation.kk: Шағын автобус purple түсті; 289 — қажетті түс емес, маршрут нөмірі.
explanation.ru: Мини-автобус фиолетовый, purple; 289 — номер маршрута, не нужный цвет.

groups.title: Local food shops
groups.instruction: Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

items.quote: Have you ever tried samphire?
items.prompt: Fish market: a handful of ____ (type of seaweed)

explanation.en: Leon recommends samphire and later spells S-A-M-P-H-I-R-E; “seaweed” is the description already supplied.
explanation.kk: Леон samphire ұсынады, кейін S-A-M-P-H-I-R-E деп айтады; seaweed — берілген сипаттама.
explanation.ru: Леон советует samphire и затем диктует S-A-M-P-H-I-R-E; seaweed — уже указанное описание.

items.quote: I'd prefer a melon — it's bigger too.
items.prompt: Organic shop: beans and a ____ for dessert

explanation.en: Shannon prefers a melon because mangoes may not be ripe; mango is the rejected suggestion.
explanation.kk: Шеннон mango піспеуі мүмкін болғандықтан melon қалайды; mango ұсынысы қабылданбаған.
explanation.ru: Шеннон предпочитает melon, потому что манго может быть неспелым; mango — отвергнутый вариант.

items.quote: The owner also sells a lot of spices there that you can put in a curry, and things like coconut.
items.prompt: Organic shop: spices and ____

explanation.en: Leon says the shop sells spices and coconut for a curry; the beans belong in the other table column.
explanation.kk: Леон карриге дәмдеуіш пен coconut сатылатынын айтады; бұршақ басқа бағанға қатысты.
explanation.ru: Леон говорит, что для карри продают специи и coconut; фасоль относится к другой колонке.

items.quote: Well — not that, but they have a whole range of tarts and the best are the strawberry ones.
items.prompt: Bakery: a ____ tart

explanation.en: The recommended tarts are strawberry; chocolate cake was asked about but is not sold there.
explanation.kk: Strawberry бәліші ұсынылады; шоколадты торт сұралды, бірақ ол жерде сатылмайды.
explanation.ru: Рекомендуют клубничные пироги, strawberry; шоколадный торт спрашивали, но его там нет.

groups.title: Shopping
groups.instruction: Complete the table below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.

parts.context: Two friends discuss local food shops and shopping for a meal.

transcript.text: Hi Shannon — how are you settling into your new flat?
transcript.speaker: LEON

transcript.text: Really well, thanks.
transcript.speaker: SHANNON

transcript.text: You look like you're going shopping.
transcript.speaker: LEON

transcript.text: Yes, I am.
transcript.speaker: SHANNON

transcript.text: My cousins are coming to stay for a couple of days, and I have to cook for them.
transcript.speaker: SHANNON

transcript.text: Well, there are plenty of places to buy food in Kite Place — it's the area by the harbour.
transcript.speaker: LEON

transcript.text: Oh, OK, I'll find that on the map.
transcript.speaker: SHANNON

transcript.text: Thanks.
transcript.speaker: SHANNON

transcript.text: What sort of food do you need to get?
transcript.speaker: LEON

transcript.speaker: SHANNON

transcript.text: Well, there's a really good fish market there.
transcript.speaker: LEON

transcript.text: Oh great — where is it exactly?
transcript.speaker: SHANNON

transcript.text: It's at the far end of Kite Place, so you have to go over the bridge and then it's on the right.
transcript.speaker: LEON

transcript.text: OK — is it open all day?

transcript.text: It doesn't close until four, but I'd recommend going earlier than that — it does run out of some things.
transcript.speaker: LEON

transcript.text: Oh, I don't want that to happen.
transcript.speaker: SHANNON

transcript.text: As long as you get there by 3.30, you should be fine.
transcript.speaker: LEON

transcript.text: It's only 11 now, so plenty of time.
transcript.speaker: LEON

transcript.text: Right.
transcript.speaker: SHANNON

transcript.text: I know, it's 'Rose'.
transcript.speaker: LEON

transcript.text: That's a nice name.
transcript.speaker: SHANNON

transcript.text: Yeah — it sells vegetables and quite a lot of other stuff.
transcript.speaker: LEON

transcript.text: And where's that?
transcript.speaker: SHANNON

transcript.text: Anyway, now it's a restaurant upstairs, but the ground floor has two shops either side of the entrance and it's the one on the left.

transcript.text: That's easy enough.
transcript.speaker: SHANNON

transcript.text: You can't miss it — there's also a big sign on the pavement so you can look for that.
transcript.speaker: LEON

transcript.text: Fine!
transcript.speaker: SHANNON

transcript.text: I guess if I need anything else, I'll have to go to the supermarket.

transcript.speaker: LEON

transcript.text: It's purple and the number is 289.
transcript.speaker: LEON

transcript.text: Thanks, that's great.
transcript.speaker: SHANNON

transcript.text: So what do you need to get at the fish market?
transcript.speaker: LEON

transcript.text: The salmon is always very good and the shellfish.
transcript.speaker: LEON

transcript.text: I'm going to make a curry, I think, and I need about 12 prawns for that.
transcript.speaker: SHANNON

transcript.text: They'll have plenty of those.
transcript.speaker: LEON

transcript.text: OK.
transcript.speaker: SHANNON

transcript.text: Have you ever tried samphire?
transcript.speaker: LEON

transcript.text: No — what's that?
transcript.speaker: SHANNON

transcript.text: It's a type of seaweed.
transcript.speaker: LEON

transcript.text: I just ask for a handful and you fry it in butter.
transcript.speaker: LEON

transcript.text: It's delicious!
transcript.speaker: LEON

transcript.text: Oh, I might try that — how do you spell it?

transcript.text: It's S-A-M-P-H-I-R-E.
transcript.speaker: LEON

transcript.text: Great — it's always good to try something different.
transcript.speaker: SHANNON

transcript.text: Yeah.
transcript.speaker: LEON

transcript.text: I'll see what beans they have in the organic shop and I think I'll get something for dessert there.
transcript.speaker: SHANNON

transcript.text: How about a mango?
transcript.speaker: LEON

transcript.text: I'm not sure — they're not always ripe.
transcript.speaker: SHANNON

transcript.text: I'd prefer a melon — it's bigger too.
transcript.speaker: SHANNON

transcript.text: Good idea.
transcript.speaker: LEON

transcript.text: The owner also sells a lot of spices there that you can put in a curry, and things like coconut.
transcript.speaker: LEON

transcript.text: Oh, that's very helpful.
transcript.speaker: SHANNON

transcript.text: I'll have a look.
transcript.speaker: SHANNON

transcript.text: No problem.
transcript.speaker: LEON

transcript.text: I know bread doesn't really go with curry but I always like to have some in case.
transcript.speaker: SHANNON

transcript.text: As I said — all the bread is home-made and there's lots of variety.
transcript.speaker: LEON

transcript.text: I like the brown bread myself.
transcript.speaker: LEON

transcript.text: Mm, sounds good.

transcript.text: They sell other things there too.

transcript.speaker: SHANNON

transcript.speaker: SHANNON

items.quote: This is a chance for deaf children to share their reading experiences with author Madeleine Gordon, who is herself hearing impaired. 'Just do it' is a practical workshop led by the well-known illustrator Mark Keane.
items.prompt: Superheroes

explanation.en: The event is for deaf children, identifying disability as the key feature.
explanation.kk: Іс-шара естімейтін балаларға арналған; негізгі белгі — есту кемістігі.
explanation.ru: Мероприятие для глухих детей; ключ — нарушение слуха.

items.quote: He'll take participants on a magical journey to faraway lands with an opportunity for aspiring actors to do some role play. 'Count on me' is an inspiring and entertaining look at the issues of friendship for 13—14-year-olds.
items.prompt: Just do it

explanation.en: Although an illustrator leads it, participants do role play rather than drawing.
explanation.kk: Жетекші — иллюстратор, бірақ балалар сурет салмай, рөл ойнайды.
explanation.ru: Художник ведёт занятие, но дети занимаются ролевой игрой, а не рисованием.

items.quote: He'll take participants on a magical journey to faraway lands with an opportunity for aspiring actors to do some role play. 'Count on me' is an inspiring and entertaining look at the issues of friendship for 13—14-year-olds.
items.prompt: Count on me

explanation.en: The specified age group is 13–14; friendship is discussed but not specifically new relationships.
explanation.kk: 13–14 жас көрсетілген; достық талқыланады, бірақ тек жаңа қатынас емес.
explanation.ru: Указан возраст 13–14 лет; обсуждают дружбу, но не только новые отношения.

items.quote: This is a creative writing workshop encouraging children to describe situations where young people experience loneliness.
items.prompt: Speak up

explanation.en: Children write about loneliness, an unhappy feeling.
explanation.kk: Балалар жалғыздық — жағымсыз сезім туралы жазады.
explanation.ru: Дети пишут об одиночестве — неприятном чувстве.

items.quote: It recently received the gold medal at the Waterford Awards.
items.prompt: Jump for joy

explanation.en: Nina Karan received a gold medal, so the workshop is led by a prize-winning author.
explanation.kk: Нина Каран алтын медаль алған; жетекші — жүлделі автор.
explanation.ru: Нина Каран получила золотую медаль; ведущая — автор с наградой.

items.quote: Nina will get children to celebrate the word 'joy' by writing a poem. 'Sticks and stones' is the beautifully illustrated picture book for young readers about a community who organise an African-Caribbean festival to help local children learn about their Jamaican roots.
items.prompt: Sticks and stones

explanation.en: The African-Caribbean festival helps children learn about Jamaican roots.
explanation.kk: Балалар афро-кариб фестивалі арқылы ямайкалық тамырын таниды.
explanation.ru: Дети узнают о ямайских корнях через афро-карибский фестиваль.

items.quote: It's good to read more advanced books to them as it helps to develop their vocabulary If you don't have time for this, then let them listen to audio books.

Allow children to listen to audio books.
Get recommendations from librarians.
Give children a choice about what they read.
Only read aloud to children until they can read independently.

explanation.en: Audio books and librarians’ recommendations are advised; stopping reading aloud is called a mistake.
explanation.kk: Аудиокітап пен кітапханашының көмегі ұсынылады; дауыстап оқуды тоқтату қате делінген.
explanation.ru: Советуют аудиокниги и помощь библиотекарей; прекращать чтение вслух названо ошибкой.

parts.context: A presenter interviews a book festival organiser about workshops and reading.

transcript.text: The children's book festival is coming up again soon and here to tell us all about it is the festival's organiser, Jenny Morgan.
transcript.speaker: PRESENTER

transcript.text: So tell us what we can expect this year, Jenny.
transcript.speaker: PRESENTER

transcript.text: Well, as usual we've got five days of action-packed exciting events for children, with writers coming from all over the country getting involved.
transcript.speaker: JENNY

transcript.text: Just to give you an idea of what's on offer in the workshops, first of all, there's a very special event called Superheroes.
transcript.speaker: JENNY

transcript.text: This is a chance for deaf children to share their reading experiences with author Madeleine Gordon, who is herself hearing impaired. 'Just do it' is a practical workshop led by the well-known illustrator Mark Keane.
transcript.speaker: JENNY

transcript.text: He'll take participants on a magical journey to faraway lands with an opportunity for aspiring actors to do some role play. 'Count on me' is an inspiring and entertaining look at the issues of friendship for 13—14-year-olds.
transcript.speaker: JENNY

transcript.text: It looks at some of the friendships described in popular books and asks participants to compare these with their own experiences. 'Speak up' is part of a series of workshops on the subject of mental health.
transcript.speaker: JENNY

transcript.text: This is a creative writing workshop encouraging children to describe situations where young people experience loneliness.
transcript.speaker: JENNY

transcript.text: A recent survey revealed that children can be lonely even when they're at home with their families. 'Jump for joy', as many of you will know, is the heart-warming, best-selling story by Nina Karan about a young girl's trip to visit her relatives in India.
transcript.speaker: JENNY

transcript.text: It recently received the gold medal at the Waterford Awards.
transcript.speaker: JENNY

transcript.text: Nina will get children to celebrate the word 'joy' by writing a poem. 'Sticks and stones' is the beautifully illustrated picture book for young readers about a community who organise an African-Caribbean festival to help local children learn about their Jamaican roots.
transcript.speaker: JENNY

transcript.text: This will be a musical event where children will have the chance to play steel drums.
transcript.speaker: JENNY

transcript.text: This is bound to be very popular, so please book as soon as possible.
transcript.speaker: JENNY

transcript.text: Thanks Jenny.
transcript.speaker: PRESENTER

transcript.text: That all sounds really interesting.
transcript.speaker: PRESENTER

transcript.text: I'm just wondering if you have a favourite book you could recommend for our readers?
transcript.speaker: PRESENTER

transcript.text: It's hard to choose, but Alive and Kicking is definitely worth mentioning.
transcript.speaker: JENNY

transcript.text: You won't have heard of the writer as it's her first book — which is really impressive.
transcript.speaker: JENNY

transcript.text: It's basically the teenage diary of a boy from Somalia who comes to live in the UK.
transcript.speaker: JENNY

transcript.text: It deals with the serious issue of immigration and all the challenges the boy has to face at school and with the language barrier, etc.
transcript.speaker: JENNY

transcript.text: Usually, books like this are quite sad, but this one actually made me cry with laughter.
transcript.speaker: JENNY

transcript.text: On each page, there are simple but hilarious black and white stick drawings of the boy with his friends and teachers.
transcript.speaker: JENNY

transcript.text: At the end of each diary entry, there are new English words the boy learns each day, which may help develop some children's vocabulary.
transcript.speaker: JENNY

transcript.text: I think my kids would enjoy that.
transcript.speaker: PRESENTER

transcript.text: What about any advice for parents on how to encourage their children to read more?
transcript.speaker: PRESENTER

transcript.text: Well, this is something I get asked about a lot.
transcript.speaker: JENNY

transcript.text: There are so many distractions for kids these days that it can be hard to find time for reading.
transcript.speaker: JENNY

transcript.text: One thing I'd say is to make time to sit down with your child and share books with them.
transcript.speaker: JENNY

transcript.text: A lot of parents give up reading aloud to their children as soon as they learn to read independently, but this is a mistake.
transcript.speaker: JENNY

transcript.text: It's good to read more advanced books to them as it helps to develop their vocabulary If you don't have time for this, then let them listen to audio books.
transcript.speaker: JENNY

transcript.text: Often, they'll want to read books they've listened to for themselves.
transcript.speaker: JENNY

transcript.text: I think it's a good idea to make a mental note of the type of books your child is reading — often they just read the same genre all the time, which can get a bit boring.
transcript.speaker: JENNY

transcript.text: You can introduce new authors and genres to them.
transcript.speaker: JENNY

transcript.text: Librarians should be able to help you with this.
transcript.speaker: JENNY

transcript.text: Well Jenny, I think that's really useful.
transcript.speaker: PRESENTER

items.quote: They listen to what I say, and I gave them a test last week and the results weren't too bad, but there's no real engagement.
items.prompt: How does Clare feel about the students in her Year 12 science class?

options.text: worried that they are not making progress
challenged by their poor behaviour in class
frustrated at their lack of interest in the subject

explanation.en: Results and discipline are acceptable; she is frustrated by their lack of engagement.
explanation.kk: Нәтижелері жаман емес, тәртібі қалыпты; оны қызығушылықтың жоқтығы қынжылтады.
explanation.ru: Результаты неплохие и дисциплина нормальная; её огорчает отсутствие интереса.

items.quote: OK, but you'd also need to have access to the children's medical records and I don't think people would be happy about that; confidentiality would be an issue.
items.prompt: How does Jake react to Clare’s suggestion about an experiment based on children’s diet?

options.text: He is concerned that the results might not be meaningful.
He feels some of the data might be difficult to obtain.
He suspects that the conclusions might be upsetting.

explanation.en: Confidential medical records may be hard to obtain; the conclusions could be significant.
explanation.kk: Медициналық жазба құпия, сондықтан дерек алу қиын; қорытынды маңызды болуы мүмкін.
explanation.ru: Медицинские записи конфиденциальны, поэтому получить данные трудно; выводы могли бы быть значимыми.

items.quote: But if we found out that, say, a particular diet affects the health of animals, the same thing wouldn't necessarily be true for people. would it?
items.prompt: What problem do they agree may be involved in an experiment involving animals?

options.text: Any results may not apply to humans.
It may be complicated to get permission.
Students may not be happy about animal experiments.

explanation.en: Results for animals may not apply to people; permission is described as straightforward.
explanation.kk: Жануар нәтижесі адамға сәйкес келмеуі мүмкін; рұқсат алу оңай.
explanation.ru: Результаты для животных могут не подходить людям; разрешение получить просто.

items.quote: In fact, maybe the focus could be on whether mice can control their own diet.
items.prompt: What question do they decide the experiment should address?

options.text: Are mice capable of controlling their food intake?
Does an increase in sugar lead to health problems?
How much do supplements of different kinds affect health?

explanation.en: The final focus is whether mice control their own diet; supplements were an earlier suggestion.
explanation.kk: Соңғы мақсат — тышқан өз тамақтануын реттей ме; қоспалар бастапқы идея еді.
explanation.ru: Окончательная цель — выяснить, регулируют ли мыши собственное питание; добавки были предварительной идеей.

items.quote: Like, you could give some of the mice the chance to be more active. running on a wheel or something, and the others just sit around and don't do much.
items.prompt: Clare might also consider doing another experiment involving

options.text: other types of food supplement.
different genetic strains of mice.
varying amounts of exercise.

explanation.en: Clare prefers Jake’s activity idea over her own alternatives involving food or genetics.
explanation.kk: Клэр Джейктің белсенділік идеясын тағам мен генетика нұсқаларынан қызығырақ санайды.
explanation.ru: Клэр считает идею Джейка об активности интереснее своих вариантов еды и генетики.

groups.title: Science experiment for Year 12 students
groups.instruction: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

items.quote: And all young ones. not a mixture of old and young.
items.prompt: Choose mice which are all the same ____.

explanation.en: Only young mice are selected, indicating the same age; size refers to the groups.
explanation.kk: Тек жас тышқан алынады, яғни жасы бірдей; size топ көлеміне қатысты.
explanation.ru: Берут только молодых мышей, то есть одного возраста; size относится к размеру групп.

items.quote: You could use food colouring, that wouldn't hurt them.
items.prompt: Divide the mice into two groups, each with a different ____. Then put each group in a separate cage.

explanation.en: Food colouring distinguishes the groups; size or water is not the distinguishing feature.
explanation.kk: Топтар тағам бояуымен ажыратылады; көлемі не суы өзгермейді.
explanation.ru: Пищевой краситель различает группы; не меняют размер или воду.

items.quote: It might be better to give them something like cereal with it.
items.prompt: Feed group A commercial mouse food. Feed group B the same, but also sugar contained in ____.

explanation.en: The additional sugar is supplied in cereal, rather than water.
explanation.kk: Қосымша қантты жармада, cereal, беруді ұсынады; суда емес.
explanation.ru: Дополнительный сахар предлагают в хлопьях, cereal; не в воде.

items.quote: So you need something called a weighing chamber to stop the mice from running away.
items.prompt: Take measurements using an electronic scale. Place them in a weighing chamber to prevent ____.

explanation.en: The chamber stops mice running away, paraphrased as escape.
explanation.kk: Камера тышқанның қашуына жол бермейді; escape — running away баламасы.
explanation.ru: Камера не даёт мышам убежать; escape — перефразирование running away.

items.quote: So once we've measured the weight gain of each mouse we can work out the average for each group. as well as the standard deviation.
items.prompt: Do all necessary ____.

explanation.en: They calculate the mean and standard deviation, requiring calculations rather than changes.
explanation.kk: Орташа мән мен стандартты ауытқу есептеледі — calculations; changes емес.
explanation.ru: Вычисляют среднее и стандартное отклонение — calculations, а не просто changes.

parts.context: Two trainee teachers plan a science experiment using mice.

transcript.text: Hi Jake.
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: How are you getting on with the practical teaching?
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: It's harder than I expected, but I've got some great classes.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: How about you?
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: Not brilliant.
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: I'm really struggling with my Year 12 science class.
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: Are they hard to control?
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: Well, I don't have discipline problems as such.
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: It's just that they don't seem to think that science has anything to do with their lives.
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: It's depressing.
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: They listen to what I say, and I gave them a test last week and the results weren't too bad, but there's no real engagement.
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: Right.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: And as part of my teaching practice, I have to design an experiment for them to do.
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: I was wondering about something on the children's diets ... you know, asking them to record what they eat and maybe linking it to their state of health.
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: Mmm.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: Let's think.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: So your methodology would involve the children recording what they eat.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: OK, but you'd also need to have access to the children's medical records and I don't think people would be happy about that; confidentiality would be an issue.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: If you could get the right data, the conclusions might be significant, but I suspect it's not going to be easy.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: Right.
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: Have you thought about doing an experiment using animals?
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: Wouldn't that be upsetting for the children?
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: Well, the animals don't have to be harmed in any way.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: It could just be an experiment where they're given a certain diet and the effects are observed.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: Would I have to get permission to use animals?
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: Yes, you'd have to submit an outline of the experiment and fill in a form, but it's quite straightforward.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: But if we found out that, say, a particular diet affects the health of animals, the same thing wouldn't necessarily be true for people. would it?
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: No that's true, but the findings for any experiment are going to be limited.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: It's inevitable.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: I suppose so.
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: So what animals could I use to investigate the effects of diet?
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: Mice?
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: Yes.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: You'd need experimental mice — ones that have been specially bred for experiments.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: OK, so what will your experiment be investigating exactly?
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: Well, something to do with nutrition.
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: So maybe we could look at food supplements ... things like extra iron and extra protein, and their impact on health.
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: Mmm.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: That might be rather broad.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: Maybe just look at the effects of one supplement, like sugar, on the health of the mice?
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: In fact, maybe the focus could be on whether mice can control their own diet.
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: So, what happens when they have access to more sugar, that they don't really need?
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: Exactly.
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: Do they eat it or do they decide to leave it?
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: Great.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: Then later on, you could do a follow-up experiment adding another variable.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: Like, you could give some of the mice the chance to be more active. running on a wheel or something, and the others just sit around and don't do much.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: Or I could repeat the experiment but change the type of food I provided . or use mice with a different genetic structure.
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: But I think your idea would be more interesting, I might think about that some more.
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: So can I talk through a possible procedure for the experiment where mice are given a sugar supplement?
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: Sure.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: I did a similar experiment in college actually.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: Great.
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: So how many mice would I need?
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: I'd say about 12.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: And all young ones. not a mixture of old and young.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: OK.
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: And I'd need two groups of equal sizes, so six in each group.
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: And how would I tell them apart?
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: I suppose I could put some sort of tag on one group ... or just mark them in some way?
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: You could use food colouring, that wouldn't hurt them.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: Perfect.
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: Then each group would go into a separate cage, and one group, let's call them group A, would be the control group.
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: So they'd just have ordinary mouse food.
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: I suppose you can buy that?
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: Yes, it comes in dry pellets.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: And the other group would have the same as the first group, but they'd also have the extra sugar.
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: Would you just give them straight sugar?
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: It might be better to give them something like cereal with it.
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: Mmm.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: Then you'd need to weigh the mice, I should think once a week.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: And you'd need an electronic balance.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: But we can't hold them on the balance, or it'd affect the reading.
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: Exactly.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: So you need something called a weighing chamber to stop the mice from running away.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: It sounds complicated, but actually you can just use a plastic box with holes in the top.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: OK.
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: So once we've measured the weight gain of each mouse we can work out the average for each group. as well as the standard deviation.
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: And then see where we go from there.
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: That sounds cool, I think the students will enjoy it.
transcript.speaker: CLARE

transcript.text: Yes.
transcript.speaker: JAKE

transcript.text: One thing .
transcript.speaker: JAKE

items.quote: Threads and microfibres detach from synthetic clothing every time they're put in a washing machine, and these find their way into the water system.
items.prompt: Fibres from some ____ during washing

explanation.en: Threads and microfibres detach from synthetic clothing during washing; factory waste is another source.
explanation.kk: Жуу кезінде талшық синтетикалық clothing киімнен бөлінеді; фабрика қалдығы — басқа көз.
explanation.ru: При стирке волокна отделяются от синтетической одежды, clothing; отходы фабрик — другой источник.

items.quote: There is evidence that microplastics harm small creatures in a variety of ways, such as by damaging their mouths, or by impairing their ability to feed, for example when microplastics get lodged in their digestive system.
items.prompt: They cause injuries to the ____ of wildlife and affect their digestive systems.

explanation.en: Microplastics can damage animals’ mouths; the digestive system is the separate effect already mentioned.
explanation.kk: Микропластик жануарлардың mouths мүшесін зақымдайды; ас қорыту жүйесі — берілген басқа әсер.
explanation.ru: Микропластик повреждает рты животных, mouths; пищеварительная система — отдельное, уже указанное воздействие.

items.quote: What's more, salt and many kinds of seafood have also been found to contain microplastics.
items.prompt: They enter the food chain, e.g., in bottled and tap water, ____ and seafood.

explanation.en: Salt is named alongside seafood as containing microplastics; water is already supplied before the gap.
explanation.kk: Salt теңіз өнімдерімен бірге аталады; су бос орынның алдында берілген.
explanation.ru: Соль, salt, названа наряду с морепродуктами; вода уже дана перед пропуском.

items.quote: In many countries, including here in the UK, there is legislation which prevents manufacturers from adding plastic microbeads to shower gels. facial cleansers and toothpaste.
items.prompt: They may not affect human health, but they are already banned in skin cleaning products and ____ in some countries.

explanation.en: The ban covers shower gels, facial cleansers and toothpaste; the first two are grouped as skin-cleaning products.
explanation.kk: Тыйым гельге, бет тазартқышқа және toothpaste өніміне қатысты; алғашқы екеуі тері тазартқыш ретінде біріктірілген.
explanation.ru: Запрет касается гелей, средств для лица и toothpaste; первые два объединены как средства для кожи.

items.quote: What's more, many of the fertilisers used by both farmers and gardeners contain microplastics.
items.prompt: Microplastics enter the soil through the air, rain and ____.

explanation.en: Fertilisers used by farmers and gardeners may contain microplastics and introduce them into soil.
explanation.kk: Фермер мен бағбан қолданатын fertilisers микропластикті топыраққа енгізуі мүмкін.
explanation.ru: Удобрения, fertilisers, применяемые фермерами и садоводами, могут переносить микропластик в почву.

groups.title: Microplastics — sources and effects
groups.instruction: Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.

items.quote: By feeding on soil, they mix nutrients into it, thereby making it more fertile.
items.prompt: Earthworms are important because they add ____ to the soil.

explanation.en: Earthworms mix nutrients into soil, making it more fertile; use the plural form as spoken.
explanation.kk: Жауынқұрт топыраққа nutrients араластырып, құнарландырады; көпше түрін сақтаңыз.
explanation.ru: Дождевые черви перемешивают питательные вещества, nutrients, в почве; сохраните множественное число.

items.quote: The researchers set out to discover whether the introduction of microplastics into the soil — and the subsequent ingestion of these by earthworms — would impact soil quality and ultimately inhibit plant growth.
items.prompt: The study aimed to find whether microplastics in earthworms affect the ____ of plants.

explanation.en: The study tested whether microplastics ultimately inhibit plant growth; soil quality is an intermediate effect.
explanation.kk: Зерттеу микропластик өсімдіктің growth өсуін тежей ме деп тексерді; топырақ сапасы — аралық әсер.
explanation.ru: Изучали, мешает ли микропластик росту растений, growth; качество почвы — промежуточное воздействие.

items.quote: The result was that the worms lost weight rapidly.
items.prompt: The study found that microplastics caused ____ loss in earthworms.

explanation.en: The worms lost weight rapidly; “weight loss” in the notes paraphrases “lost weight”.
explanation.kk: Құрттар weight салмағын тез жоғалтқан; weight loss — lost weight баламасы.
explanation.ru: Черви быстро теряли вес, weight; weight loss перефразирует lost weight.

items.quote: The team also discovered that there was an increase in the amount of acid found in the soil. and this was attributed mainly to the microplastic particles from conventional HDPE plastic.
items.prompt: The study found a rise in the level of ____ in the soil.

explanation.en: The researchers found more acid in the soil; HDPE names the plastic associated with that increase.
explanation.kk: Зерттеушілер топырақта acid артқанын анықтады; HDPE — соған байланысты пластик атауы.
explanation.ru: Исследователи нашли больше кислоты, acid, в почве; HDPE — связанный с этим пластик.

items.quote: That is, when soil becomes impoverished by the presence of microplastics, not only ecosystems but also the whole of society are negatively impacted.
items.prompt: The study concluded that changes to soil damage both ecosystems and ____.

explanation.en: The conclusion says both ecosystems and the whole of society are negatively affected.
explanation.kk: Қорытындыда экожүйе мен бүкіл society теріс әсер алатыны айтылады.
explanation.ru: В выводе говорится, что страдают экосистемы и всё общество, society.

groups.title: Microplastics in the soil — a study by Anglia Ruskin University
groups.instruction: Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.

parts.context: A lecturer discusses sources and effects of microplastics.

transcript.text: In today's lecture, I'm going to be talking about microplastics.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Microplastics are tiny pieces of plastic smaller than five millimetres in size.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Recently there's been a greater awareness that there are large quantities of plastic waste — big and small — in the environment.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: The amount of plastic waste in the oceans has received widespread attention, but far less is known about the effects of microplastics in freshwater and particularly in soil.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Microplastics can enter the environment via a number of different sources.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Threads and microfibres detach from synthetic clothing every time they're put in a washing machine, and these find their way into the water system.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Other sources include big pieces of plastic waste that are already in the environment, and these break down into microscopic particles over a period of time.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: On a larger scale, factory waste is another route, as are tyres which wear down as cars, lorries and so on travel along road surfaces.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: We already understand some of the impacts of microplastics from studies involving fish and other animals.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: There is evidence that microplastics harm small creatures in a variety of ways, such as by damaging their mouths, or by impairing their ability to feed, for example when microplastics get lodged in their digestive system.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Surprisingly perhaps, it is likely that humans consume microplastics, as these have been detected in a wide range of food and drink products, including bottled water, as well as in water that comes direct from the tap.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: What's more, salt and many kinds of seafood have also been found to contain microplastics.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: However, it's important to underline that there is not yet conclusive proof that microplastics cause significant harm to people.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: In many countries, including here in the UK, there is legislation which prevents manufacturers from adding plastic microbeads to shower gels. facial cleansers and toothpaste.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: It is very difficult to accurately estimate the total amount of microplastic particles in the soil as they can be hard to detect, but we do know they are carried in the air and deposited in the soil by rain.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: What's more, many of the fertilisers used by both farmers and gardeners contain microplastics.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: A team from the Anglia Ruskin University in Cambridge has carried out a study of the effects of microplastics on the digestive tracts of earthworms.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: These worms, which live in topsoil, are an essential component of our agricultural system.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: By feeding on soil, they mix nutrients into it, thereby making it more fertile.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: The researchers set out to discover whether the introduction of microplastics into the soil — and the subsequent ingestion of these by earthworms — would impact soil quality and ultimately inhibit plant growth.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: The short answer was, yes, it did.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: After placing three different types of microplastic particles into the soil, they planted perennial rye grass.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: The particles of microplastic, which included biodegradable PLA and conventional high-density polyethylene, or HDPE, were then ingested by the earthworms in the soil.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: The result was that the worms lost weight rapidly.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: What's more, a lower percentage than normal of the rye grass seeds germinated, and the researchers concluded that this was a direct result of the earthworms being unable to fulfil their normal role in making soil more fertile.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: The team also discovered that there was an increase in the amount of acid found in the soil. and this was attributed mainly to the microplastic particles from conventional HDPE plastic.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: The conclusions of the study make for very interesting reading — I've included the reference in the notes to give you at the end of this session.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: To summarise, the authors proposed the idea that we need to regard soil as we would regard any other process in nature.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: This means we should accept the implications of soil being dependent on decaying and dead matter constantly being passed through the bodies of earthworms.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: That is, when soil becomes impoverished by the presence of microplastics, not only ecosystems but also the whole of society are negatively impacted.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER
